name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
alt: Grand Duchy of Lithuania and Ruthenia

successors.name: House of Jagiellon
successors.text: the whole Grand Duchy of Cliopatria's last shape, drawn inside the Jagiellonian realm from 1450

ledger.x: 1236: Mindaugas rules a Lithuanian state after the Battle of Saule.
1236: Lithuania annexes Navahrudak and Hrodna.
1239: the Lithuanians briefly capture Smolensk.
1240: 'Grand Prince Yaroslav Vsevolodovich expelled them the following year' (Smolensk page).
1240: Polotsk becomes a vassal of Lithuania.

1250: Cliopatria draws Minsk inside Lithuania for 1250-1259 and, from 1260 to 1313, as its own Principality of Minsk row (98,755 km2, covering Minsk, Polotsk and Vitebsk) whose area the infobox ('1260: 200,000 km2') counts with Lithuania's 90,777 km2.
1251: Lithuania becomes a kingdom.
1263: Mindaugas is assassinated and the Kingdom of Lithuania ends.
1279: the capital moves to Kernavė.
1307: Lithuania annexes Polotsk.
1307: the vassalage of Polotsk ends in annexation.
1314: Cliopatria draws Minsk inside Lithuania again as its Minsk row ends in 1313.
1314: the Minsk land is drawn inside the Lithuanian shape again as Cliopatria's Minsk row ends in 1313 (see the gain of 1314).
1316: Gediminas moves the capital to Trakai.
1318: Algirdas marries Maria of Vitebsk and becomes Prince of Vitebsk.
1321: Gediminas captures Kyiv.
1323: Vilnius becomes the capital.
1326: Cliopatria draws Pinsk inside Lithuania as the Pinsk row ends in 1325.
1326: Cliopatria draws Turov inside Lithuania as the Turov row ends in 1325.
1326: Cliopatria adds Brest and the Volhynian border to Lithuania.
1326: a strip on Masovia's north-eastern edge goes to Lithuania.
1349: Poland and Hungary occupy Galicia-Volhynia and Volhynia is contested.
1352: Lithuania holds Lutsk and eastern Volhynia.
1356: Algirdas captures Smolensk and Bryansk.
1357: Chernigov and Bryansk come under Lithuania.
1359: Algirdas 'launched an attack, regaining control of Smolensk and Rzhev while taking control of Mstislavl' (Smolensk page; the year 1359 follows from the page's 'the following year' after 1358).
1362: Lithuania fights the Golden Horde for the south.
1363: the fighting ends in a Lithuanian victory at Blue Waters.
1363: Lithuania takes Kyiv, Podolia and the road to the Black Sea from the Golden Horde.
1366: the treaty of fall 1366 divides Volhynia.
1375: about 40,000 km2 in the north (30.6-34.9 E, 55.8-57.7 N) pass from Smolensk's shape to Lithuania's.
1375: Cliopatria adds Kamianets and Podolian land in the south.
1395: Vytautas captures Smolensk.
1398: Vytautas cedes Samogitia to the Teutonic Knights.
August 1399: Vytautas is crushed at the Vorskla and loses the Black Sea coast.
1401: Smolensk revolts and leaves Lithuania.
1404: Vytautas retakes Smolensk.
May 1409: Samogitia rises against the Order.
1 February 1411: the Peace of Thorn returns Samogitia to Lithuania for two lifetimes.
1 February 1411: the war of 1409-1411 ends with the Peace of Thorn.
1414: the Hunger War over the north bank of the Neman and Memel.
1422: the Treaty of Melno ends the Samogitian dispute.
1431: Cliopatria drops Kamianets, most of Podolia and a corner of Volhynia (1431 is Cliopatria's shape year).
25 June 1431: Poland invades Volhynia.
1 September 1431: a truce at Staryi Chortoryisk ends the Lutsk War.
31 August 1432: the coup that makes Sigismund Kęstutaitis Grand Duke splits the state.
1438: Švitrigaila withdraws to Moldavia and his side ends.
1449: the Grand Duchy's last Cliopatria shape ends and the lands pass into the Jagiellonian realm.

wars.name: Battle of Durbe (Livonian Order against Samogitians and Lithuanians)
wars.outcome: The Order lost Skuodas in 1259 and Durbe in 1260; Mindaugas 'broke peace with the Livonian Order' in 1261.

wars.name: Lithuanian wars against the Teutonic and Livonian Orders under Gediminas
wars.outcome: Gediminas 'allied himself with the Tatars against the Teutonic Order in 1319', made peace with the Livonian Order on 2 October 1323, and the war resumed after the Order murdered his delegate in 1325; the page records a battle at Bayernburg in 1337.

wars.name: Battle of Blue Waters
wars.outcome: Lithuanian victory over the Golden Horde: Kyiv, Podolia and a large part of today's Ukraine under Lithuanian control, with access to the Black Sea.

wars.name: Galicia-Volhynia Wars (succession wars of 1340-1392)
wars.outcome: After Yuri II Boleslav was poisoned in April 1340 Poland, Hungary and Lithuania fought over his lands: a truce 'rather favourable to the Lithuanians' in fall 1352, a treaty in fall 1366 that left Liubartas 'only eastern Volhynia with Lutsk', Lithuanian…

wars.name: Lithuanian-Muscovite War (1368-1372)
wars.outcome: Algirdas 'besieged Moscow in 1368 and 1370'; no border change is recorded on the page.

wars.name: Battle of the Vorskla River
wars.outcome: A decisive Golden Horde victory under Edigu and Temür Qutlugh: Vytautas barely escaped and 'Lithuania loses the Black Sea coast and southern part of the Wild Fields to the Tatars'.

wars.name: Great War (Polish-Lithuanian-Teutonic War of 1409-1411)
wars.outcome: The Samogitian uprising of May 1409 grew into war; after Grunwald (June 1410) the Peace of Thorn of 1 February 1411 gave Samogitia to Lithuania for the lifetimes of Jogaila and Vytautas and returned Dobrzyń Land to Poland.

wars.name: Hunger War
wars.outcome: An inconclusive war over the north bank of the Neman and Memel after the Knights refused Makrai's award of May 1413; the dispute was 'not resolved until the Treaty of Melno in 1422'.

wars.name: Lutsk War
wars.outcome: Poland invaded Volhynia on 25 June 1431 after Vytautas's death; a truce at Staryi Chortoryisk on 1 September 1431 ended it, and the Knights were defeated at Dąbki on 13 September.

wars.name: Lithuanian Civil War (1432-1438)
wars.outcome: Sigismund Kęstutaitis, backed by Poland, defeated Švitrigaila, backed by the Teutonic Knights, at Wiłkomierz in September 1435; Švitrigaila surrendered in 1437 and withdrew to Moldavia in 1438; Sigismund was assassinated in 1440 and Casimir IV approved as…

certainty.note: Frontiers with the Rus' principalities, the steppe and the Orders are approximate throughout; the Samogitian border with the Teutonic Order is fixed by treaty only from the Treaty of Melno in 1422 (Memel stayed with the Order), the one…
